question: For a patient on 60 mg oral morphine per day as background analgesia, an appropriate breakthrough (rescue) dose is 10 mg oral morphine (i.e., one-sixth of the total daily dose).

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The WHO breakthrough dose formula is 1/6th of the total 24-hour opioid dose, available every 2–4 hours PRN. For 60 mg/day morphine, 10 mg every 2–4 hours PRN is the correct calculation — a standard prescribing competency (AS8.4).
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The standard breakthrough dose is 1/6th (approximately 10–17%) of the total daily opioid dose, available every 2–4 hours as needed. This allows adequate rescue without overshooting. For 60 mg/day, a 10 mg breakthrough is textbook correct.
